searchText: Reminder! CL call in 26 hours https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/443 First part will be about kintsugi/the-merge. EL teams, please join us! This has been said often, but how would you convince those large staking providers to do so? Ideally they wouldn't need convincing, but choose to do so out of rational self-interest. Game theoretically, I think this might point to the threat of no bailouts for a majority client mass slashing not being credible enough. i.e. option 1 -> provider does 'the right thing' and moves to a minority client = certainty of no bailout for client mass slashing option 2 -> provider stays with the majority client = chance of bailout for mass client slashing because of disruptiveness to the entire ecosystem. but how can you make it credible without having a worst-case scenario play out in reality 🤔 Reminder -- CL call in 50 minutes Just a thought - you could raise an issue in the GitHub repos of the large staking providers as a suggestion to switch over some of their clients when spinning up new validators and in the issue submitted raise up the goal of client diversification. Might not be able to get them to switch all the way but at least gets the thinking of the importance of client diversity as a topic of discussion within their teams. While I am not a dev team member of StakeWise I am a vocal community member and could advocate this to the dev team for their consideration. Forgive me if I’m speaking out of place here. Could somebody send me a link for the CL call please DVs are still very new and not production ready yet imo. Block production in DVs is a tricky question because you have MEV extraction on the table as an externality that can compromise stable DV operation. The current plan with Obol is to leverage flashbots' blind block production architecture, such that no entity in the DV knows what they are proposing. Call notes: https://hackmd.io/@benjaminion/ryBR2ip3Y - discussion got pretty technical at times and the notes quality drops off a bit there; check the recording for the detail.

excerpts.author: pieterastra
excerpts.content:
This has been said often, but how would you convince those large staking providers to do so?
Ideally they wouldn't need convincing, but choose to do so out of rational self-interest.
Game theoretically, I think this might point to the threat of no bailouts for a majority client mass slashing not being credible enough.
i.e. option 1 -> provider does 'the right thing' and moves to a minority client = certainty of no bailout for client mass slashing
option 2 -> provider stays with the majority client = chance of bailout for mass client slashing because of disruptiveness to the entire ecosystem.
